claims.text: Regions: cervical (7), thoracic (12), lumbar (5), sacrum (5 fused), coccyx (3–4 fused).
claims.quote: Spine: 5 regions: cervical (7), thoracic (12), lumbar (5), sacrum (5 fused), coccyx (3–4 fused)

claims.text: C1 and C2: C1 (atlas) has no body; C2 (axis) carries the odontoid process (dens).
Surface landmarks: the C7 spinous process (vertebra prominens) at the base of the neck; spine of the scapula at about T3; PSIS dimples at about S2; inferior angle of the scapula at about T7.
claims.quote: C7 spinous process = vertebra prominens (most prominent, base of neck) - Spine of scapula ~T3 - PSIS dimples ~S2 highest iliac crests ~L4 (supracristal/Tuffier’s line → identify L3–L4 or L4–L5 for LP) - I. angle of scapula ~T7

claims.text: Tuffier's line: the highest points of the iliac crests are at about L4, used to find the L3–L4 or L4–L5 space for lumbar puncture.
claims.quote: highest iliac crests ~L4 (supracristal/Tuffier’s line → identify L3–L4 or L4–L5 for LP)

claims.text: Deep intrinsic back muscles: erector spinae (iliocostalis, longissimus, spinalis) and transversospinalis (semispinalis, multifidus, rotatores).
claims.quote: Deep intrinsic: erector spinae (iliocostalis, longissimus, spinalis) + transversospinalis (semispinalis, multifidus, rotatores)

claims.text: Ligaments: the anterior longitudinal ligament (front of the bodies) limits extension; the posterior longitudinal ligament (back of the bodies, inside the canal) limits flexion; the ligamentum flavum joins adjacent laminae, and its hypertrophy causes spinal stenosis.
claims.quote: A. longitude: body (front), full length → limit extend - P. longitude: body (back) inside canal → limit flex Ligamentum flavum: connects adj laminae (hypertrophy → spinal stenosis)

claims.text: Discs: the nucleus pulposus absorbs and distributes axial load; the annulus fibrosus resists tension and torsion.
claims.quote: Central nucleus pulposus: gelatinous, water-rich → absorb/dist axial load annulus fibrosus: concentric lamellae of fibrocartilage → resist tension/torsion

claims.text: Disc aging: the nucleus dehydrates and loses height (degenerative disc disease); annular tears let the nucleus herniate and compress a nerve root.
claims.quote: Aging: nucleus dehydrates + loses height (DDD) - annular tears → nucleus herniates → compress n. root

claims.text: Spinal nerves: 31 pairs (8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral, 1 coccygeal), each with a dorsal (sensory) and ventral (motor) root.
claims.quote: each = dorsal (sensory) + ventral (motor) root -31 pairs: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral, 1 coccygeal
claims.locator: Anatomy section, Spine: Spinal n. & plexuses

claims.text: Plexuses: cervical C1–C4 (phrenic nerve from C3–C5); brachial C5–T1 (upper limb); lumbar L1–L4 (femoral and obturator); sacral L4–S4 (sciatic, the largest nerve, dividing into tibial and common fibular).
claims.quote: Plexuses: cervical: C1–C4; phrenic from C3–C5 - Brachial: C5–T1; upper limb Lumbar: L1–L4; femoral & obturator - Sacral: L4–S4; sciatic = largest n. → tibial & common fibular
